itineraries.title: Durham Saturday — Market, Malcolm, Ballpark
itineraries.theme: One walkable downtown, three very different rooms, and a 6:45 first pitch you can stroll to
itineraries.drive_time: Park once. The market, the ballpark and the tour meeting point are all within a mile of Foster Street; only the Nasher needs a car (8 minutes each way).
itineraries.cost_range: $25–$60 per person. The market and the gallery talk are free; the tour is $15 and Bulls tickets start around $13.
itineraries.overview: 86°F with scattered storms in the forecast, so this route keeps a roof within reach all day. The Durham Farmers' Market opens at eight and thins out by ten, the Nasher's Mapping Malcolm talk is free and air-conditioned at noon, and the walking tour lands you back downtown in time to eat before the Bulls.

morning.title: Durham Farmers’ Market
morning.notes: Go early — the good produce and the pastry stalls are gone well before noon. The DCP Pavilion has cover if it is already raining.

afternoon.title: Gallery Talk: Exploring Mapping Malcolm with Najha Zigbi-Johnson
afternoon.notes: Free, indoors, about an hour. Najha Zigbi-Johnson on the Mapping Malcolm exhibition; the rest of the Nasher is worth the extra half hour afterwards.

afternoon.title: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour
afternoon.notes: Ninety minutes on foot from CCB Plaza through downtown's Black history. Wear real shoes and bring water — very little of it is shaded.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Norfolk Tides
evening.notes: Norfolk Tides in town for a four-game set. The Blue Monster side gets the late sun; the third-base concourse is the shadier half.

food.vegan_dish: Ask the bakery stalls which loaves and hand pies are made without butter or egg — several are, and they will tell you straight
food.vegetarian_dish: A breakfast pastry and coffee from the market vendors
food.notes: 501 Foster St. Eat at the pavilion tables so you are not carrying a plate around the stalls.

food.vegan_dish: At least one counter usually plates a fully plant-based bowl — ask each kitchen directly, the lineup rotates
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza or a vegetable-forward plate from whichever kitchen is open
food.notes: 530 Foster St, two minutes from the market. Air conditioning and several kitchens under one roof, no reservation.

food.place: Ballpark concessions or Jack Tar on Parrish
food.vegan_dish: The DBAP has a veggie-dog stand; Jack Tar can build a plate without dairy if you ask
food.vegetarian_dish: Ballpark pretzels and fries, or a diner grilled cheese before the game
food.notes: Eat before you go in if you want a real meal — concession lines are worst in the half hour before first pitch.

alternatives.leg: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour (4 PM, entirely outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the full ninety minutes on foot and finish at CCB Plaza.
alternatives.rain: Storms are a real possibility. Swap in the Nasher's own galleries, which you are already at, or the free Museum of Durham History on Main Street.

alternatives.leg: Durham Bulls vs. Norfolk Tides (6:45 PM, open-air ballpark)
alternatives.good_weather: Sit down the third-base line for shade and the tobacco-warehouse backdrop.
alternatives.rain: If the game goes to a delay, Ira Glass is at DPAC the same evening at 7:30 (event 952eb56a19ec) — five minutes' walk from the ballpark.

practical_notes: 86°F and scattered storms. Every outdoor leg here has an indoor pivot within a few blocks, which is the point of anchoring the day downtown.
The Durham Farmers' Market runs 8 AM–noon at 501 Foster Street; the Wednesday market is a separate, smaller thing.
Nasher admission is free on this talk; parking in the Nasher lot is free too.
Bulls parking decks fill from about an hour before first pitch — the Chapel Hill Street decks are the reliable fallback.

itineraries.title: Chapel Hill — Planetarium Day into Giant Puppets
itineraries.theme: Air-conditioned dome shows through the hottest hours, then an outdoor amphitheatre at dusk
itineraries.drive_time: About 15 minutes of driving total. Morehead and the Forest Theatre are a mile apart on the same side of campus; Cat's Cradle is 8 minutes further into Carrboro.
itineraries.cost_range: $35–$70 per person, most of it the planetarium tickets and the Paperhand donation.
itineraries.overview: This is the shape a 86°F day with afternoon storms wants: spend the middle of the day inside a dome, come out when the light goes long, and end at the Forest Theatre, which is outdoors but wooded and cool. If the sky holds, Cat's Cradle picks up the night.

morning.title: Saturday Science Sparks: Warmer Climates with the Data-Driven EnviroLab
morning.location: 222 E. Franklin Street, Chapel Hill, NC, Chapel Hill, NC
morning.notes: Hands-on climate science for kids and adults at Morehead, free with the day's programming. A good warm-up before the ticketed dome shows.

afternoon.title: We Are Stars
afternoon.location: 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill, NC 27514
afternoon.notes: Half an hour under the dome, narrated by Andy Serkis. Book ahead on a Saturday — the early-afternoon shows sell out first.

afternoon.title: From Earth to the Universe
afternoon.location: 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill, NC 27514
afternoon.notes: A full-dome tour of the sky. Between the two shows there is time for coffee on Franklin Street without moving the car.

evening.title: Paperhand Puppet Intervention: The Wild Wisdom of the World
evening.location: 123 S Boundary St, Chapel Hill, NC 27514
evening.notes: Openers at 6:20, Paperhand at 7:00. Arrive well before the opener — seating is grass and stone, and the good spots go early. Bring a cushion.

evening.title: Sincere Engineer: The Probable Claws Tour Stay Inside, Smug LLC
evening.notes: If you skip the puppets or want a second act, Sincere Engineer's Probable Claws tour is in the Back Room, eight minutes away in Carrboro.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel plate or the hummus-and-pita breakfast, both dairy-free as served
food.vegetarian_dish: Spanakopita or a feta-and-egg pita
food.notes: 410 W Franklin St. Quick counter service, five minutes from Morehead.

food.vegan_dish: Chana masala or the daily vegan thali — the kitchen labels vegan dishes on the board
food.vegetarian_dish: Saag paneer or the vegetarian thali
food.notes: 431 W Franklin St, in Courtyard. Genuinely good for both diets and used to being asked.

food.place: Al's Burger Shack or Neal's Deli in Carrboro
food.vegan_dish: Al's will build the veggie burger without cheese or mayo; Neal's does a plant-forward sandwich most days
food.vegetarian_dish: Veggie burger, or Neal's pimento cheese biscuit
food.notes: Eat before the Forest Theatre — there is no food at the amphitheatre and nothing near it.

alternatives.leg: Paperhand Puppet Intervention at the Forest Theatre (6:20 PM, open-air)
alternatives.good_weather: Get there by 5:30, spread a blanket high on the stone terraces and watch the light drop through the trees.
alternatives.rain: The Forest Theatre has no cover at all. If storms roll through, the 4:30 PM Carolina Skies show at Morehead is the same evening's sky indoors, and Cat's Cradle's 8 PM show is unaffected.

alternatives.leg: Morehead dome shows (1:30 and 3:00 PM, indoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Still worth it — this is the coolest room in Chapel Hill on an 86°F afternoon.
alternatives.rain: No change. This is already the rain plan.

practical_notes: Morehead's shows are ticketed separately from the free hands-on programming; buy dome tickets online before you drive over.
Forest Theatre parking is street-only on Country Club Road and fills fast — arriving 90 minutes early is normal for Paperhand.
Paperhand seating is grass and stone terraces. Bring a blanket or a low chair, and bug spray.
Cat's Cradle's Back Room is a separate, smaller room from the main hall — check which door your ticket names.

itineraries.title: Raleigh Saturday — Almost All of It Free
itineraries.theme: A market, two free museum tours and one $10 walk, with an optional amphitheatre night at the end
itineraries.drive_time: About 20 minutes of driving. North Hills to downtown is 12 minutes; everything after that is within four blocks of Bicentennial Plaza.
itineraries.cost_range: $10–$25 per person for the day, or add a Chance the Rapper ticket if you want the evening.
itineraries.overview: Three of the four daytime stops cost nothing. The Museum of Natural Sciences has free general admission and runs two guided tours on Saturdays, and the Black History walking tour from the Pope House is $10 and the best-value hour downtown. Storms are possible, and almost all of this is indoors.

morning.title: Midtown Farmers' Market
morning.location: 4111 Main at North Hills St, Raleigh, NC 27609
morning.notes: Producers' market on The Commons at North Hills, 8 to noon. Cooking demos most Saturdays; free parking in the decks.

morning.title: Downtown Raleigh Black History Tour
morning.notes: Starts at the Dr. M.T. Pope House Museum on South Wilmington. $10, roughly 90 minutes, entirely on foot.

afternoon.title: The ICONS Tour
afternoon.notes: Free hour-long tour of the museum's signature specimens. Immediately after the walking tour and four blocks north.

afternoon.title: Museum Untold Tour
afternoon.notes: Two hours behind the scenes at the Museum of Natural Sciences. Free but popular — sign up at the desk when you arrive in the morning.

evening.title: Chance the Rapper: Coloring Book 10 Year Anniversary Tour
evening.notes: Coloring Book turns ten and the tour is at Red Hat, a ten-minute walk from the museum. Skip it and the day costs $10 total.

food.vegan_dish: Several bakery and prepared-food stalls run plant-based items — ask, the roster changes weekly
food.vegetarian_dish: Pastry and coffee from the market stalls
food.notes: The Commons at North Hills. Eat there rather than carrying food downtown.

food.vegan_dish: Ask each counter directly — at least one kitchen usually has a fully plant-based bowl
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza, or a vegetable plate from whichever kitchen is open
food.notes: 500 E Davie St, eight minutes from the museum. Air conditioning and no reservation needed.

food.place: Vita Vite Midtown or the Red Hat food trucks
food.vegan_dish: Vita Vite plates a vegan board on request; the amphitheatre trucks usually include one plant-based option
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese board, flatbread, or truck fries and arepas
food.notes: If you are going to Red Hat, eat downtown first — inside prices are what you would expect.

alternatives.leg: Downtown Raleigh Black History Tour (10 AM, entirely on foot)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the whole route; the Pope House itself is worth the extra fifteen minutes afterwards.
alternatives.rain: Storms are in the forecast. The Museum of Natural Sciences is free, four blocks away and open 10–5 — the ICONS Tour at 11 works as a straight substitute.

alternatives.leg: Chance the Rapper at Red Hat Amphitheater (7 PM, open-air)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk down from the museum and eat on Fayetteville Street on the way.
alternatives.rain: Red Hat is uncovered. ComedyWorx runs a family-friendly stand-up show at 7 PM on West Morgan Street if the evening washes out.

practical_notes: The Museum of Natural Sciences has free general admission every day — only some programmes are ticketed.
Museum Untold Tour spots are limited and go at the front desk; ask when you arrive for the ICONS Tour.
Red Hat has a clear-bag policy and the gates open about an hour before the show.
Downtown parking decks are free on Saturdays; street meters are not enforced.

itineraries.title: Pittsboro — Sculpture Farm, Tigers, Piano
itineraries.theme: A 40-minute drive out of Raleigh into Chatham County for a free sculpture show on a working farm
itineraries.drive_time: 40 minutes from Raleigh, 25 from Chapel Hill. Once you are in Chatham the legs are 10–15 minutes apart; JimGin Farm is on a gravel road southwest of town.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$45 per person. The market and the sculpture show are free; the tiger rescue tour is ticketed.
itineraries.overview: Come Out and Play is in its 23rd year — more than 50 artists showing sculpture across a 17-acre homestead, free food, live music, noon until dark. It is the reason to make the drive. Build the rest of the day around it: the Chatham Mills market first, Carolina Tiger Rescue's twilight tour after, and piano at The Sycamore to finish.

morning.title: Chatham Mills Farmers Market
morning.notes: Saturday market at Chatham Mills, on the way in from Chapel Hill. Small, good, and done by noon.

afternoon.title: Come Out and Play Sculpture Show
afternoon.notes: 150 Wild Horse Run. Free, runs noon until dark, and the hosts feed you. Wear shoes you do not mind getting dusty — it is a farm, not a gallery.

evening.title: Twilight Tours at Carolina Tiger Rescue
evening.notes: Carolina Tiger Rescue's twilight tour is when the cats are actually awake. Book ahead; walk-ups are not guaranteed.

evening.title: Live Piano Music at The Sycamore
evening.notes: The Sycamore at Chatham Mills, back in town. Quiet end to the day, no cover.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk coffee and the avocado toast without the feta — the counter is used to the ask
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit or a pastry
food.notes: Downtown Pittsboro, opens early. Fuel before the market.

food.place: Come Out and Play's own tables
food.vegan_dish: The hosts put out free food each day and it is usually vegetable-heavy — ask what is dairy-free before you plate up
food.vegetarian_dish: Whatever is on the farm tables; there is normally a meatless spread
food.notes: Free food is part of the show's whole idea. Bring water anyway — it is a farm in August.

food.vegan_dish: Ask for a build-your-own sandwich with hummus and vegetables, no cheese or aioli
food.vegetarian_dish: Grilled cheese or the veggie sandwich
food.notes: On Hillsboro Street in town. Simple, reliable, and open late enough after the tiger tour.

alternatives.leg: Come Out and Play Sculpture Show (noon until dark, entirely outdoors on a farm)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk the whole 17 acres and stay for the live music as the light goes.
alternatives.rain: Scattered storms are forecast and there is almost no cover on the farm. The Chatham Mills buildings in town stay open, and the Carolina Tiger Rescue tour runs rain or shine.

alternatives.leg: Twilight Tours at Carolina Tiger Rescue (5 PM, outdoors on gravel paths)
alternatives.good_weather: The 5 PM slot is when the cats move; go then rather than earlier.
alternatives.rain: Tours run in light rain — check the rescue's own page before driving out, and keep The Sycamore's piano set as the fallback.

practical_notes: Pittsboro is inside the Triangle ring but it is still a 40-minute drive from Raleigh — this is a whole-day trip, not an add-on.
JimGin Farm is at 150 Wild Horse Run, down a gravel road. Phone signal is patchy; screenshot the directions.
Carolina Tiger Rescue tours must be booked in advance and are not suitable for very young children.
The sculpture show repeats every Saturday through September 26 if this weekend does not work.

itineraries.title: Hillsborough — Last Fridays Art Walk
itineraries.theme: Nineteen galleries open late on one small-town main street, free, with a telescope at the end
itineraries.drive_time: 35 minutes from Raleigh, 20 from Chapel Hill or Durham. Once you are on Churton Street everything is on foot.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$35 per person. The art walk and the star party are free; the money goes on dinner.
itineraries.overview: Last Fridays is the best free night out in Orange County and it runs 5:30 to 9. Nineteen venues open with artist receptions, demonstrations and live music, the Makers Market sets up on the Old Courthouse lawn, and the Live on the Lawn series covers everything from drums to puppets. The Burwell School's star party at 7:30 gives the evening a second act.

afternoon.title: Musical Notes at Margaret Lane Gallery
afternoon.notes: Margaret Lane Gallery's curated group show — one of the receptions that opens with the art walk. Start here and work north up Churton.

evening.title: Last Fridays & the Art Walk
evening.notes: Free, and free parking, which is not nothing in a town this size. Start at the Old Courthouse lawn and let the Makers Market point you at the rest.

evening.title: Star Party!
evening.notes: Telescopes on the Burwell School lawn. Clear sky is not guaranteed tonight, so treat it as a bonus rather than the plan.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk coffee and a plain bagel with jam
food.vegetarian_dish: Bagel and cream cheese
food.notes: If you are making a full day of it, start here before the shops open.

food.vegan_dish: Ask which sides are cooked without pork fat — the slaw and the hush puppies vary by day, and they will tell you
food.vegetarian_dish: A plate of sides: mac and cheese, slaw, hush puppies
food.notes: 236 S Nash St. Not a vegan destination, but honest about what is in the pot.

food.vegan_dish: Ask the kitchen for the vegetable plate built without butter; the bar menu changes often
food.vegetarian_dish: Pimento cheese and a vegetable plate
food.notes: On Churton Street, inside the art-walk footprint. Live music most weekends.

alternatives.leg: Last Fridays & the Art Walk (5:30–9 PM, street-level, mostly outdoors between venues)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk the whole of Churton Street and stay for Live on the Lawn.
alternatives.rain: Showers and thunderstorms are likely tonight. The nineteen venues are all indoors — the art walk survives rain, the Makers Market and the lawn performances do not.

alternatives.leg: Star Party at the Burwell School Historic Site (7:30 PM, open lawn)
alternatives.good_weather: Stay past dark; the sky over Hillsborough is genuinely better than the Triangle's.
alternatives.rain: Cancelled by cloud, not just rain. Fright Night at Eagle Lodge is the same evening and indoors.

practical_notes: 5:30 to 9 PM, free, and parking downtown is free too.
Details for each month firm up the week before — the Hillsborough Arts Council page is the one to check on the day.
Showers and thunderstorms are likely: the gallery receptions are indoors, the lawn programming is not.
Hillsborough is inside the Triangle ring but it is a 35-minute drive from Raleigh — plan the evening around one trip, not two.

itineraries.title: Cary Friday — Night Market, Drums, Nineties Rock
itineraries.theme: Three free things in one downtown park, then a 10-minute drive to a lakeside amphitheatre
itineraries.drive_time: Everything downtown is one walk from the Academy Street decks. Koka Booth is 10 minutes south, and it has its own paid lots.
itineraries.cost_range: $0 for the downtown half; add a Koka Booth ticket if you want the concert.
itineraries.overview: Downtown Cary Park stacks three free events into one Friday evening — the Night Market at five, a West African drum and fire show at seven, and a swing dance with lessons at half past. If you would rather end the night with Blues Traveler, Gin Blossoms and Spin Doctors, Koka Booth is ten minutes away and starts at seven.

afternoon.title: Cary Night Market
afternoon.notes: Triangle artisans, food and drink in the park until nine. Go early if you actually want to buy something.

evening.title: One Tribe Drum Circle and Fire Show
evening.notes: Caroleeena & Friends on the Old Library site next to the Ivey-Ellington House — drumming, dancing and a fire show. Free.

evening.title: Discover Dance: Swing Session
evening.notes: Charleston and swing with lessons throughout, so turning up alone and knowing nothing is the expected case.

evening.title: Blues Traveler & Gin Blossoms with Spin Doctors
evening.notes: The alternative ending: Blues Traveler and Gin Blossoms with Spin Doctors on the lawn at Koka Booth. Pick this or the park, not both.

food.vegan_dish: Ask which of the morning pastries are made without butter — usually at least one is
food.vegetarian_dish: Quiche or a breakfast pastry
food.notes: 6490 Tryon Rd. Worth the detour if you are starting the day in Cary.

food.vegan_dish: Ask the kitchen to build the veg sandwich without aioli or cheese
food.vegetarian_dish: Grilled cheese or the vegetable sandwich
food.notes: Academy Street, two minutes from the park.

food.vegan_dish: Vendors rotate weekly; ask before you queue, several trucks run plant-based menus
food.vegetarian_dish: Arepas, pizza or noodles from the market trucks
food.notes: Eat in the park. If you are going to Koka Booth instead, eat before you drive — lawn concessions are slow.

alternatives.leg: Cary Night Market and the park programming (5–9 PM, all outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the whole run: market, drums, then the swing session on the plaza.
alternatives.rain: Showers and thunderstorms are likely tonight. The Cary Theater is a two-minute walk and has a comedy show at 8 PM; the park events are the ones that cancel.

alternatives.leg: Blues Traveler & Gin Blossoms at Koka Booth (7 PM, lawn and covered seating)
alternatives.good_weather: Lawn tickets and a blanket by the lake is the way to see this one.
alternatives.rain: The reserved section is covered; the lawn is not. Buy reserved if the radar looks bad, or stay downtown and take the indoor comedy show.

practical_notes: All three downtown events are free and within one block of each other in and around Downtown Cary Park.
The Academy Street and Walker Street decks are free and the closest parking to the park.
Koka Booth is 10 minutes south at 8003 Regency Parkway with its own paid lots; leaving after an encore takes a while.
87°F and storms likely — this is the evening where checking radar at 4 PM actually changes your plan.

itineraries.title: Durham Sunday — Chapel, Day Game, Chamber Music
itineraries.theme: The one properly sunny day of the week, spent on Duke's campus and at a 1:05 first pitch

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.drive_time: Duke's campus to the ballpark is 10 minutes; Koskinen Stadium is 5 minutes back onto West Campus. Roughly 30 minutes of driving all day.
itineraries.cost_range: $25–$70 per person depending on how many ticketed legs you take. The chapel tour is free.
itineraries.overview: 89°F and mostly sunny — the first day this week without storms in the forecast, so this is the one to spend outside. A print workshop and a free chapel tour fill the morning, the Bulls play a 1:05 matinee, and the evening splits between chamber music indoors and Duke men's soccer under lights.

morning.title: Printmaking workshop
morning.notes: Outer Loop Arts, $25, two hours and you leave with prints. Book ahead — these fill.

morning.title: Public Tour of Duke Chapel
morning.notes: Free 45-minute tour of Duke Chapel. Cool stone in the middle of an 89°F day, which is the real argument for it.

afternoon.title: Durham Bulls vs. Norfolk Tides
afternoon.notes: Sunday matinee against Norfolk. Full sun for most of it — the third-base side gets shade first.

evening.title: MALLARMÉ — Where Cultures Meet: Chamber Music by American Women
evening.notes: Mallarmé Music playing chamber works by American women. Two hours, indoors, and it overlaps the back end of the ballgame — pick one.

evening.title: Duke Men's Soccer vs Georgetown
evening.notes: Duke against Georgetown at Koskinen. Free for the general public most nights; the 6 PM start means the worst of the heat has gone.

food.vegan_dish: Monuts keeps vegan doughnuts on the rack most mornings and marks them
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit or a cake doughnut
food.notes: 1002 9th St. Queue moves fast; go before 10 on a Sunday.

food.vegan_dish: Pie Pushers will build a pizza without cheese; the DBAP has a veggie dog
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese pizza, ballpark pretzel, fries
food.notes: Eat before the gates if you want anything better than concession food.

food.vegan_dish: Guasaca's black-bean arepa without cheese; Nanataco does a mushroom taco with no dairy
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese arepa, or the veggie taco plate
food.notes: Both are quick and a few minutes from Koskinen — useful either side of the soccer.

alternatives.leg: Durham Bulls matinee (1:05 PM, open-air, full sun)
alternatives.good_weather: 89°F and mostly sunny. Sunscreen, and sit on the third-base side for the first shade.
alternatives.rain: Only a slight chance today. If it does turn, the Mallarmé chamber concert at 3 PM (event d04bd5ea4d3c) is indoors and the same afternoon.

alternatives.leg: Duke Men's Soccer vs Georgetown (6 PM, Koskinen Stadium)
alternatives.good_weather: Best leg of the day — the heat is off by six and the stadium is small enough to see everything.
alternatives.rain: Slight chance of evening storms. Duke Chapel and the Nasher both stay open late enough to be a fallback on campus.

practical_notes: 89°F and mostly sunny — the only day this week without storms in the daytime forecast.
The Bulls matinee at 1:05 and the Mallarmé concert at 3:00 overlap. Take one; the itinerary lists both so you can choose.
Duke Chapel tours are free and start inside the chapel; no booking needed.
Duke's Koskinen Stadium parking is free on Sundays in the Blue Zone lots.

itineraries.title: Tuesday at 96°F — Stay Inside Until Dark
itineraries.theme: The hottest day of the week, planned entirely around air conditioning and two free science talks after sundown
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown Raleigh in the day, then 25 minutes to Carrboro or 25 to Durham for the evening — pick one, they run at the same time.
itineraries.cost_range: $10–$30 per person. Both evening talks are free; the IMAX ticket is the only fixed cost.
itineraries.overview: 96°F and sunny is not a day for a farmers market. Marbles' IMAX runs films from 10:15, the Museum of Natural Sciences has free admission and a midday Science TODAY talk, and after dark the Triangle's two free science-in-a-bar nights both land: Carolina Science Cafe in Carrboro and Astronomy on Tap in Durham.

morning.title: Animal Kingdom 3D
morning.notes: Marbles IMAX, first film of the day. The five-storey screen and the coldest room downtown.

afternoon.title: Science TODAY: When Wild Animals Meet People
afternoon.notes: Free talk at the Nature Research Center on wildlife and people. Museum admission is free too, and it is a four-minute walk from Marbles.

evening.title: Carolina Science Cafe: NC’s Changing Climate
evening.location: 300 E Main St C, Carrboro, NC 27510
evening.notes: Carolina Science Cafe on North Carolina's changing climate, free, at Haw River Tap & Table in Carrboro.

evening.title: Astronomy On Tap – Science Talk & Trivia
evening.notes: Or Astronomy on Tap in Durham — short pub-friendly talks and trivia, also free. Same evening, opposite ends of the Triangle.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk latte and the vegan biscuit when it is on
food.vegetarian_dish: Biscuit with jam, or granola
food.notes: Downtown location is a few minutes from Marbles.

food.vegan_dish: Ask each stall — at least one usually has a fully plant-based bowl or a falafel plate
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza, poke without fish, or a noodle bowl
food.notes: 411 W Morgan St. Indoors, cold, and ten minutes' walk from the museum.

food.place: Haw River Tap & Table (Carrboro) or a Durham taproom
food.vegan_dish: Both venues do fries and a vegetable-forward plate; ask about butter on the vegetables
food.vegetarian_dish: Flatbread, pretzel, or a grain bowl
food.notes: Eat where the talk is — both are bar venues that serve food, and you want the table before it fills.

alternatives.good_weather: 96°F and sunny is the reason this itinerary has no outdoor daytime leg at all.
alternatives.rain: No rain expected. The plan is already the heat plan.

alternatives.leg: Carolina Science Cafe (6 PM, Carrboro) vs Astronomy on Tap (7 PM, Durham)
alternatives.good_weather: Both are free and both are indoors. Pick by which end of the Triangle you are on — they are 25 minutes apart and overlap.

practical_notes: 96°F and sunny. Nothing in this itinerary asks you to stand in it.
Museum of Natural Sciences admission is free; Marbles IMAX is ticketed separately from museum entry.
The two evening talks overlap and are 25 minutes apart — this is a choose-one, not a do-both.
Both science nights are free and neither requires registration, but seating at the Carrboro one goes early.
